newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse sees euro firm, wants strict criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse sees euro firm, wants strict criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Helmut Hesse on Tuesday called for strict observance of the economic qualification criteria for planned European monetary union (EMU).
Hesse, making a speech in the small north German town of Bodenwerder, said that "if the stability criteria are applied strictly, the group of EMU members will be small, but solid and stable."
He said that no country should be allowed to join EMU if it did not fully meet the criteria, and said this also applied to countries joining after the initial start-up date.
"The convergence criteria should remain unchanged and aimed at stability even for countries which join EMU later," he said, adding that he was "pretty sure" the euro would not be a weak currency.
Hesse said that it was also important, in order to avoid turbulence on currency markets, that the fixed parities between members countries should be set as early as possible.
EMU is due to start on January 1, 1999. (( -- Kevin Liffey, Bonn newsroom +49-228-26097160 ))
